newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada banks launch cashless Exact card project.
newsitem.headline: Canada banks launch cashless Exact card project.

text.p: A consortium of three Canadian banks launched on Tuesday what they describe as North America's first reloadable electronic cash card.

The Exact card will be tested under a pilot program set up by the Bank of Montreal, Toronto-Dominion Bank and Canada Trust, owned by CT Financial Services Inc . It will be held in Kingston, a small city about 270 km east of Toronto. "With Exact, we now have a great new alternative to cash, credit and debit cards," said Tim Hockey, vice president of core banking services for Canada Trust.

Canadians carry an estimated 46.2 million debt and credit cards while use of these cards has jumped 43 percent in the past year. A recent survey found that Canadians are the second largest users of plastic cards in the world.
"Technology is rapidly changing the face of money, providing faster, easier and more secure transactions. This is only the beginning," Hockey said.

Customers can load up to C$200 on their Exact cards at terminals in the Kingston branches of the three participating financial institutions. Load terminals will also be located in shopping malls, student campuses and selected stores.
Bank of Montreal, TD Bank and Canada Trust will initially offer the Exact card at no charge. After an introductory period, each financial institution will set a fee for its own customers.
Nearly 600 Kingston merchants have signed up for the pilot project, the statement said.
Exact is based on smart card technology developed by Belgium-based Banksys.
